text:
Karen P: Hey team, I just got an offer and moving over from my previous company. I have a 401(k) at OldCorp with a small balance. Can I roll that into Redwood's SecureRetire plan, or should I do an IRA rollover instead? Also curious if in-plan rollovers allow Roth conversions and if taxes are withheld automatically.

Mike (People Ops): Welcome aboard! Short answer: yes, we accept incoming rollovers into the SecureRetire 401(k). You can do a direct trustee-to-trustee rollover from OldCorp to SecureRetire. If you prefer an IRA thats also fine. A couple of tradeoffs: keeping it in-plan keeps things consolidated and may allow in-plan Roth conversions if the plan permits.

Jenna (Benefits Admin): Our SecureRetire setup supports both direct rollovers and in-plan Roth conversions. Steps: 1) Request a direct rollover distribution from OldCorp to SecureRetire (use our company plan ID: RW-401K-01). 2) Submit the rollover intake form to benefits@redwood.com with the OldCorp distribution paperwork. 3) If you want an in-plan Roth conversion, tick that box on the intake form and sign the tax acknowledgement.

Karen P: If I do an in-plan Roth conversion, will payroll withhold taxes automatically, or do I owe estimated taxes?

Finn (Payroll): Payroll does NOT withhold federal income tax automatically for in-plan Roth conversions on rollover amounts. The converted amount counts as taxable income for the year, so we recommend setting aside funds or increasing withholding on your regular paycheck. You may also want to make estimated tax payments to avoid penalties.

Karen P: Are there fees or blackout windows I should expect during the rollover?

Jenna (Benefits Admin): SecureRetire charges no inbound rollover fees on our side. OldCorp might have an outbound distribution processing fee — check their paperwork. Typical transfer timing: 7-21 business days depending on custodian. We try to coordinate so there's minimal investment blackout, but small windows can occur.

Mike (People Ops): Also FYI: if your previous plan had employer matching vesting still in progress, vested portion can be rolled over; unvested employer contributions generally cannot be rolled until vested per old plan rules. Check OldCorp's SPD for vesting schedule.

Karen P: Good point. And what about loan balances? If I had an outstanding 401(k) loan at OldCorp, can that be rolled or paid off?

Jenna (Benefits Admin): Outstanding loans typically must be repaid or treated as a distribution before rollover. Some plans allow loan transfers but it's rare. OldCorp should indicate whether the loan becomes due upon separation. If its a deemed distribution, you may have taxes/penalties. Work with OldCorp first.

Kevin (SecureRetire Bot): Automated notice: To initiate a transfer, use the rollover portal at https://secure-retire.com/rollover and enter plan ID RW-401K-01. For in-plan Roth conversions, you will need to complete Form IR-Convert-01 (attached in portal).

Karen P: One last Q  can I split the rollover (partial) and leave some money at OldCorp?

Mike (People Ops): Yes, partial rollovers are allowed. Indicate the amount on the OldCorp distribution form and on our intake. Partial rollovers can be handy if youre unsure or need to preserve certain investment options at the old custodian.

Finn (Payroll): If you do an in-plan Roth conversion, let payroll know the tax year and approximate converted amount so we can flag for year-end reporting.

Karen P: Perfect, thanks everyone. Ill pull the OldCorp paperwork and submit the intake form.

Jenna (Benefits Admin): Happy to help - ping us if you want a quick walkthrough of the portal.

Karen P: Appreciate it :party_parrot:
